harmful.name: Sodium Benzoate
harmful.description: Used in soft drinks and juices. Can react with Vitamin C to form benzene (carcinogen).

harmful.name: Sodium Nitrite
harmful.description: Used in processed meats like sausages and ham. Linked to colorectal cancer risk.

harmful.name: Tartrazine
harmful.description: Synthetic yellow dye used in candies and drinks. Linked to hyperactivity in children.

harmful.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
harmful.description: Orange-yellow dye. Linked to allergic reactions and hyperactivity.

harmful.name: Allura Red AC
harmful.description: Red dye used in snacks and drinks. Linked to hyperactivity in children.

harmful.name: Titanium Dioxide
harmful.description: Used to whiten foods. May cause DNA damage; banned in the European Union.

harmful.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
harmful.description: Common flavor enhancer. May cause headaches, sweating and sensitivity in some people.

harmful.name: Aspartame
harmful.description: Artificial sweetener in diet foods. Controversial; classified as possibly carcinogenic by WHO (2023).

harmful.name: BHA (Butylated Hydroxyanisole)
harmful.description: Prevents rancidity in fats. Listed as a possible carcinogen.

harmful.name: BHT (Butylated Hydroxytoluene)
harmful.description: Used in cereals and fats. May disrupt hormonal function.

moderate.name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
moderate.description: Natural vitamin C. Generally safe; used to preserve color and freshness.

moderate.name: Citric Acid
moderate.description: Naturally found in citrus fruits. Generally safe in normal food quantities.

moderate.name: Lecithin
moderate.description: Usually derived from soy or sunflower. Generally safe but may cause soy allergy reactions.

moderate.name: Mono and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
moderate.description: Used in baked goods and margarine. May contain hidden trans fats.

moderate.name: Guar Gum
moderate.description: Derived from guar beans. May cause bloating and digestive discomfort.

moderate.name: Xanthan Gum
moderate.description: Produced by bacterial fermentation. Generally safe; may affect digestion in large amounts.

moderate.name: Pectin
moderate.description: Natural plant fiber from fruit peels. Generally safe and beneficial for digestion.

moderate.name: Polyphosphates
moderate.description: Used in processed meats and seafood. High intake may affect kidney function.

moderate.name: Sucralose
moderate.description: 600x sweeter than sugar. May negatively affect gut microbiome with regular use.

moderate.name: Caramel Color
moderate.description: Some forms (Class III, IV) may contain 4-MEI, a possible carcinogen. Check the subtype.
